originalTitle: Possession review – a nightmarish plantation drama with a divisive paranormal twist
summary: Gugu Mbatha-Raw is a lawyer sent to Jamaica to get to the bottom of a mystery about an inheritance. What unfolds is an evocative story packed with horrors, past injustices – and a supernatural element that you will rate or hate
content: What do you do when a client worth £50m – thanks to family ownership of a Jamaican sugar plantation upon which a modern fortune was built – pops his clogs and is unexpectedly revealed to have cut his only child out of his will, leaving the lot to a hitherto unknown “African national” called Cudjoe East? Why, you call in your firm’s (likely only) biracial lawyer, Claudia (Gugu Mbatha-Raw), to go over to Kingston, find him and discredit him as soon as possible. “Sounds like a job for a partner, really,” replies Claudia and, promotion thus secured, duly heads out for her mother’s homeland. She may wish, before we are very far in, that she had gone for senior partnership instead. The planter’s house is one that has been appearing to her in recent nightmares that have been full of fires, terrified figures and strange symbols. But! She is a woman of the law, not superstition, so she sets the screaming Afro-gothic warnings aside and gets on with searching the house for anything that could suggest the pro-Cudjoe will is invalid and questioning the locals for any clue as to where Cudjoe himself might be. Her late client’s driver Angelo (Jeff Crossley) tells her that he introduced the pair about six months ago when his boss wanted to learn more about local history. Angelo assures her that she will not be able to talk Cudjoe into giving up his legacy. Soon Oliver (Jonny Lee Miller, in posh, nervy mode), the disinherited son, has joined her so that they can investigate and – he is divorced as well as disinherited – build sexual tension together. What follows is a dual-timeline mystery. One story unfolds in the present, another 300 years ago when the estate was staffed by enslaved people, overseen by increasingly cruel members of Oliver’s ancestral line and facing the series of rebellions known as Tacky’s War – with a supernatural inflection that allows the two increasingly to mesh. Claudia’s nightmares increase, populated perhaps by spectral members of other ancestral lines. Images and objects that appear in the dream world turn up in the house, along with documents that make the abstract horrors of colonialism concrete. The spirits with which the local people think the house, their land, their culture is infused become increasingly restless. If you believe in that kind of thing, of course – but it does become much harder to deny once Oliver has been levitated and bounced off the ceiling by an unseen force. When Claudia meets Cudjoe (Sheldon Shepherd), he is as unmoving as Angelo promised, but also claims to be nearly 300 years old – the surviving, or surviving incarnation of, Matthew, the illegitimate son (which is to say, a child conceived by the rape of an enslaved woman) of the then landowner. Matthew was promised his freedom and the estate by his father, but was denied it by Charlotte (Bel Powley), their father’s legitimate daughter. Who may or may not have hastened her father’s death from tongue cancer – strangely contracted after he cut out Matthew’s grandmother’s tongue as a punishment for possible involvement in an abortive uprising. So the past’s injustices, sufferings and legacies work themselves into and through the present. Possession is the first full-length work from Karla Crome, so far best known for her acting roles in Misfits, You, Me and the Apocalypse and most recently in Something Very Bad Is Going to Happen. It is a potent conjuring of the pervasive, enduring evils and toxicities of colonialism. It’s a powerful look at how unadmitted sins and guilt manifest themselves and whether justice for some crimes – such sprawling, normalised, heinous crimes that you begin almost to warm to those who act out of simple depravity and malevolence – can ever be done. Are reparations possible? Where does responsibility begin and end? What is better: ancestral spirit vengeance being visited upon the guilty’s descendants, or the parlaying of a boss’s modern exploitation of your skin colour for “optics” into money and promotion? For some the accumulating paranormal-mystical element will add to the dread and horror. For others, there is a danger that it obscures the truth of the story and the suffering. Where you land, I suppose, largely depends on whether you feel that ghosts and spirits are capable of thinking up and delivering any worse experiences than man seems able to conjure and visit on his fellow man. Part of me always feels that recourse to the diabolic or ineffable is a cop-out, but that is undoubtedly a vast failure of imagination on my part. But either way, Possession is a well-textured, evocative tale touching on many important questions, if never quite digging down far enough into any of them to be truly satisfying. Possession aired on Sky Atlantic and is available on Now.
chineseTitle: 《占有》评论——一部噩梦般的种植园戏剧，带有分裂的超自然现象
chineseSummary: 古古·姆巴塔-劳 (Gugu Mbatha-Raw) 是一名律师，被派往牙买加，调查有关遗产的谜团。展开的是一个令人回味的故事，充满了恐怖、过去的不公正——以及你会评价或讨厌的超自然元素
chineseContent: 当一位身价 5000 万英镑的客户——由于家庭拥有牙买加甘蔗种植园，并在该种植园上建立了现代财富——踩破木鞋，出人意料地发现他已将自己唯一的孩子从遗嘱中剔除，将遗产留给了一位名叫库乔·伊斯特 (Cudjoe East) 的迄今不为人所知的“非洲国民”时，你会怎么做？为什么，你打电话给你公司的（可能是唯一的）混血律师克劳迪娅（古古姆巴塔劳饰），去金斯顿找到他并尽快抹黑他。 “听起来确实是一份适合合伙人的工作，”克劳迪娅回答道，并在获得晋升后按时前往她母亲的祖国。在我们深入探讨之前，她可能希望自己已经成为高级合伙人。种植园主的房子是她最近在噩梦中出现的一栋房子，里面充满了火焰、恐怖的人物和奇怪的符号。但！她是一个守法的女人，而不是迷信的女人，所以她把尖叫的非洲哥特式警告放在一边，继续在房子里搜寻任何可能表明支持库乔的遗嘱无效的东西，并向当地人询问有关库乔本人可能在哪里的任何线索。她已故客户的司机安杰洛（杰夫·克罗斯利饰）告诉她，大约六个月前，当他的老板想更多地了解当地历史时，他介绍了这对夫妇。安吉洛向她保证，她无法说服库乔放弃他的遗产。很快，被剥夺继承权的儿子奥利弗（乔尼·李·米勒饰）加入了她的行列，以便他们能够调查，并与她一起制造性紧张——他离婚了，也被剥夺了继承权。接下来是一个双时间线的谜团。一个故事发生在现在，另一个故事发生在 300 年前，当时庄园里的工作人员都是奴隶，受到奥利弗祖先血统中日益残忍的成员的监管，并面临着一系列的反抗。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
